Guideline: Depend on libm3 with the cosmic feature
Description: libm3 is the Material 3 adapter for iced/libcosmic; the cosmic feature pins the aphrody-labs libcosmic fork and selects winit, GPU, X11, Wayland and accessibility stay explicit host features
Do: Add libm3 with features cosmic plus the host features the app needs (cosmic-wgpu, cosmic-wayland, cosmic-a11y)
Don't: Depend on upstream libcosmic from crates.io or a second COSMIC pin

Guideline: Use the forks built from source
Description: COSMIC, iced and libcosmic live in the repository as pinned aphrody-labs forks and are built from source; nothing is installed as a binary
Do: Build through the workspace and the build-lane cargo wrapper
Don't: Install cosmic-* or iced packages with apt, pacman or cargo install

Guideline: Start from the system product theme
Description: libm3::cosmic::system_theme reads the COSMIC theme mode and high-contrast preference and returns Theme::aphrody (product seed, Tonal Spot) in that mode and contrast
Do: Call libm3::cosmic::system_theme once at start-up and pass the Theme as the app flags
Don't: Build a Theme from a hard-coded seed or always start in light mode

Guideline: Install the translated COSMIC theme in Settings
Description: libm3::cosmic::theme translates the M3 roles, corner radii and button components into a custom cosmic::Theme without reading or changing system configuration
Don't: Mutate cosmic-config or edit the user's COSMIC theme files from the app

Guideline: Scope the root view with themed
Description: libm3::cosmic::themed applies one native theme scope to content and its overlays, so inherited controls, menus and popovers follow the M3 roles
Do: Wrap the application view once in libm3::cosmic::themed
Don't: Re-theme every widget individually or leave overlays on the system theme
Code Bad: fn view(&self) -> Element<Message> { content.into() } // overlays fall back to the system theme

Description: Theme.colors.get(Role) returns the exact M3 role; libm3::cosmic::color converts it to iced::Color
Do: Use roles (Error OnSurfaceVariant Primary) for text and fills

Description: libm3::cosmic button, surface, text_field, checkbox, switch and slider render Component styles with M3 state layers; on_press None produces a disabled button
Do: Build controls with libm3::cosmic::button(theme Component::FilledButton label Some(msg))
Don't: Style raw cosmic::widget::button with custom closures per state

Guideline: Pass the Theme to standalone controls
Description: Fields, checkboxes, switches and sliders outside a themed scope take the Theme explicitly; application composition supplies the scope at its root
Do: Pass the same libm3::Theme value to every standalone control
Don't: Create a fresh Theme per widget or per frame

Guideline: Use libm3 surfaces for cards sheets and dialogs
Description: libm3::cosmic::surface keeps the exact semantic foreground and background of cards, sheets, menus, dialogs and app bars; COSMIC private containers keep their derived colours
Do: Wrap regions in libm3::cosmic::surface with the matching Component
Don't: Paint container backgrounds with ad-hoc Container styles

Guideline: Derive navigation and panes from the window width
Description: ApplicationFamily::layout(width_dp) returns the navigation (bar, collapsed or expanded rail), panes (single, list-detail, supporting, workspace), toolbar, scrolling and edge-to-edge for 15 app families from the M3 window classes
Do: Compute the layout from the current width and the app family on resize
Don't: Hard-code a sidebar width or one layout for every window size

Description: application(theme, layout, ApplicationView) assembles title, navigation, toolbar, content and the supporting pane with the adaptive rules; a compact supporting pane belongs to the selected route
Do: Fill ApplicationView and let application place navigation and panes
Don't: Re-implement rail and pane switching per app
Code Good: libm3::cosmic::application(material, layout, ApplicationView { title, navigation, toolbar, content, supporting })

Guideline: Use Density for target size and gaps
Description: Density Touch, Desktop and Compact give target heights 48, 40 and 32 and gaps 16, 12 and 8; Theme::performance switches to Compact density and reduced motion
Do: Read theme.density.target_height() and gap(); use performance() for constrained hosts

Description: libm3::cosmic::text maps the 15 M3 type roles onto COSMIC's pinned text API (family, size, line height, weight); the app owns font loading
Don't: Set font sizes and weights by hand on each label

Guideline: Honour high contrast and keep focus visible
Description: system_theme follows the COSMIC high-contrast flag (Contrast::High); focus uses the primary role and M3 state layers; enable cosmic-a11y for AccessKit
Do: Rebuild the Theme when the system preference changes and build with cosmic-a11y
Don't: Ignore the high-contrast setting or remove the focus indicator

Description: Bars, docks, panels and launchers of the Bun OS session are native iced/libcosmic surfaces themed by libm3, never WebView or HTML
Do: Write the panel applet in Rust with libm3::cosmic
Don't: Embed a WebView or Tauri window for shell chrome

Description: Component::style(theme, Interaction) and ApplicationFamily::layout are window-system independent (no_std facade), so contrast and layout are unit-testable
Do: Assert component colours and layouts in cargo tests
Don't: Rely only on screenshots to check theme wiring
